newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil 1997 GDP growth seen at four percent - Ipea.
newsitem.headline: Brazil 1997 GDP growth seen at four percent - Ipea.

text.p: Brazil's gross domestic product (GDP) is forecast to grow four percent in 1997, down from an estimated 4.4 percent growth rate in the year to the end of September, said the Institute of Applied Economic Research (Ipea).

Ipea said the forecast in GDP growth was lowered as a result of an estimated decrease in the growth of industrial output. Ipea sees industrial production rising 4.1 percent in 1997, down from an estimated 5.2 percent in the 12 months to the end of September.
June industrial output is expected to increase 1.9 percent on May and 8.9 percent on June 1996, said Ipea, which reports to the Brazilian Planning Ministry.
Ipea said June industrial output rose strongly in comparison with the previous year because, unlike this year car production slumped last year as factories closed down for collective holidays.
The agricultural sector is expected to grow 6.4 percent in 1997, civil construction 4.2 percent and services 3.4 percent, Ipea said.
Ipea said Brazil's trade balance was expected to remain relatively stable until the end of the year and the trade deficit for 1997 should be around $10 billion.
((--Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151))
